items.name: Marmalade
items.description: Peter Schintler's flagship fine-dining room on Calle Fortaleza — regularly credited as Old San Juan's best tasting-menu experience, with a wine list that routinely wins Wine Spectator awards.
items.why_it_matters: The benchmark for upscale dining in OSJ; its 5-course format showcases hyper-local Puerto Rican ingredients with French technique — a local-meets-world-class combination rare in the Caribbean.

items.name: Pirilo Pizza Rústica
items.description: A beloved local pizza spot that has become an OSJ institution, known for its perfectly charred, thin-crust Neapolitan pies fired in a wood-burning oven with island-sourced toppings.
items.why_it_matters: Locals consistently rank this as the best pizza on the island — it fills a neighborhood dining niche that feels authentically un-touristy even steps from the cruise ship docks.

items.name: El Jibarito
items.description: A decades-old criollo institution on Calle Sol serving hefty plates of mofongo, pernil, and bacalaítos in a no-frills dining room that feels unchanged since the 1970s.
items.why_it_matters: The quintessential 'honest Puerto Rican food' lunch stop — portions are huge, prices are local, and it's been feeding both residents and in-the-know visitors for generations.

items.name: Barú Bistro & Bar
items.description: Intimate bistro on Calle Cristo with a menu that fuses Colombian, Caribbean, and Mediterranean influences — known for its ceviche flights, whole-roasted fish, and a beautifully curated rum cocktail list.
items.why_it_matters: A true neighborhood gem — its indoor-outdoor terrace setting in a colonial building is romantic and photogenic, and the kitchen takes real risks with flavor combinations that pay off.

items.name: Café Cuatro Sombras
items.description: A farm-to-cup coffee bar on Calle Cristo sourcing single-origin beans exclusively from the Cuatro Sombras estate in Yauco — serves light breakfast pastries and espresso drinks alongside bags of the island's finest coffee.
items.why_it_matters: Puerto Rican coffee is among the world's best and almost none gets exported — this is the best place in San Juan to drink it fresh-roasted from an estate that has won Cup of Excellence.

items.name: Raíces
items.description: The most polished version of traditional Puerto Rican cooking in OSJ — a festive two-story restaurant where every dish from the tostones to the mofongo relleno is executed with care and consistency.
items.why_it_matters: Where to bring visitors who want authentic criollo in a pleasant setting rather than a plastic-chair lunch spot — the rum piña coladas made tableside are a crowd-pleasing rite of passage.

items.name: La Bodeguita de Medio
items.description: A lively sister to the Havana original perched above the bay on Calle del Muelle — Cuban sandwiches, ropa vieja, and mojitos with a terrace view of the harbor and cruise ships.
items.why_it_matters: The best water-view lunch in OSJ with credible Cuban-Caribbean cooking and an atmosphere that spills from afternoon into night — the mojito program is legitimately excellent.

items.name: Señor Paleta
items.description: A tiny street-facing shop on Calle Fortaleza specializing in handmade Mexican ice cream bars in unexpected flavors like tamarind-chile, hibiscus, mango-chamoy, and coconut-guayaba.
items.why_it_matters: The best $4 dessert in Old San Juan — a cult favorite among both locals and food-media visitors, and the perfect ending to a cobblestone afternoon walk.

items.name: 1919 Restaurant
items.description: The fine-dining flagship inside the Condado Vanderbilt's sister property — chef Juan José Cuevas's tasting menu is the most rigorous expression of modern Puerto Rican gastronomy on the island.
items.why_it_matters: Cuevas trained under some of the world's top chefs and returns that expertise to Puerto Rican terroir; this is the island's most intellectually serious restaurant and a required stop for serious foodies.

items.name: Kasalta
items.type: Puerto Rican bakery / café / lunch counter
items.description: A legendary Ocean Park / Condado-adjacent bakery and café that has operated for decades — the mallorca sandwich (a sweet roll stuffed with ham, cheese, and egg) is a Puerto Rican breakfast icon.
items.why_it_matters: Barack Obama ate here during his 2011 PR visit and the photo is on the wall; it's the authentic neighborhood breakfast institution with the best pastry case in metro San Juan.

items.name: Santaella
items.type: Puerto Rican modern / casual fine dining
items.description: Chef José Santaella's flagship at La Placita de Santurce — Puerto Rican market cuisine elevated with European technique, centered on the building's century-old marketplace aesthetic.
items.why_it_matters: Ground zero for Puerto Rico's culinary renaissance — Santaella is the chef most responsible for elevating criollo cooking to fine-dining status and his namesake restaurant proves the thesis nightly.

items.name: Lote 23
items.description: An open-air food truck collective in Santurce with 15+ rotating vendors covering everything from Korean BBQ to Puerto Rican alcapurrias, craft beer, and natural wines in a festive communal setting.
items.why_it_matters: The most vibrant food-and-culture gathering space post-Maria — part of Santurce's creative revival, it mixes street art, local music, young chefs testing concepts, and an excellent craft beer lineup.

items.name: Condado Vanderbilt — Ola
items.description: José Andrés's Puerto Rico outpost inside the historic Condado Vanderbilt hotel — a Spanish-inflected seafood tasting experience with whole-roasted fish, paella, and a spectacular ocean-view dining room.
items.why_it_matters: The only José Andrés restaurant in Puerto Rico — his post-Hurricane Maria commitment to the island is well documented, and this restaurant represents his most sustained culinary presence here.

items.name: Condado Tacos
items.description: A Condado walk-up taco counter that has earned genuine local loyalty with fresh tortillas, excellent al pastor, and island-spun salsas — more than just a snappy name.
items.why_it_matters: The go-to post-beach taco stop in Condado for locals — quick, cheap, quality; a reliable anchor when you need something fast and good between the hotel strip and the lagoon.

items.name: Pikayo
items.description: Chef Wilo Benet's landmark fine-dining restaurant — the pioneer of modern Puerto Rican cuisine, blending French training with deep criollo roots into an elegant tasting experience.
items.why_it_matters: Benet is the godfather of Puerto Rican modern cooking; Pikayo has been the island's flagship fine-dining address for two decades and remains a standard-setter every serious food traveler should visit.

items.name: Avocado Bistro
items.description: The leading all-vegan restaurant in metro San Juan — serving plant-based reinventions of PR classics like vegan mofongo, jackfruit pernil, and cashew-based flans in a bright, casual space.
items.why_it_matters: Virtually the only spot in San Juan where vegetarians and vegans can get a full Puerto Rican culinary experience without compromises — the jackfruit mofongo alone justifies the visit.

items.name: Zest at The Water Club
items.description: The Water Club hotel's rooftop restaurant with panoramic views of the Atlantic — the menu leans Caribbean-influenced New American with strong island seafood and a cocktail program built around local rums.
items.why_it_matters: Delivers the best rooftop ocean view for dinner in Condado with food that actually earns its keep — the setting elevates a first-night arrival dinner into something memorable.

items.name: Casita Miramar
items.description: A beloved neighbourhood landmark in Miramar serving traditional Puerto Rican home cooking — the slow-braised oxtail, rice with pigeon peas, and flan de queso are textbook executions of the island's comfort canon.
items.why_it_matters: The insider's answer when someone asks 'where do Puerto Ricans actually eat?' — a multigenerational family restaurant with no concessions to tourist tastes and consistently excellent arroz con pollo.

items.name: El Coqui del Mar
items.description: A no-frills seafood house in the residential pocket of Condado serving market-price whole fish, chillo frito, and Puerto Rican-style shrimp in garlic sauce — frequented more by locals than hotel guests.
items.why_it_matters: Gives visitors access to the local seafood-restaurant tradition that exists independently of the hotel-strip dining machine — honest product, honest prices, and the mofongo de camarones is a highlight.

items.name: Chef Juanjo
items.description: Chef Juan José Ávila's intimate 16-seat chef's counter in Santurce — a set menu experience that changes monthly and showcases hyper-seasonal Puerto Rican ingredients through a modern lens.
items.why_it_matters: The most exciting emerging-chef dining experience in San Juan — tighter, more experimental, and more personal than the established fine-dining rooms; a dining ticket that serious food travelers seek out.

items.name: Vianda
items.type: New Puerto Rican / farm-to-table / upscale casual
items.description: Chef Francis Guzmán's market-driven restaurant focused entirely on Puerto Rican-grown ingredients — the tasting menu and à la carte both showcase root vegetables (viandas), local proteins, and island dairy.
items.why_it_matters: The most philosophically committed expression of Puerto Rican terroir dining — Guzmán sources aggressively local and the result is a menu that could exist nowhere else in the world.

items.name: Al Cuadrado Bakery
items.description: A cult-status Santurce bakery producing naturally leavened sourdough, seasonal croissants, and Puerto Rican-inflected pastries from a small open kitchen — lines form before 8am on weekends.
items.why_it_matters: The best bread in Puerto Rico, full stop — chefs around the island order from here; visiting foodies who discover it at 7am feel like they've found a secret the internet hasn't caught up to yet.

items.name: Verde Mesa
items.description: A bright, plant-forward café in Condado known for the best brunch in the neighborhood — grain bowls, avocado toasts made with real craft, daily rotating quiches, and excellent local cold-brew coffee.
items.why_it_matters: Fills the glaring brunch gap in metro San Juan's dining scene with genuine cooking care; beloved by Condado residents who want something lighter than fried plantains on a Sunday morning.

items.name: Cocina al Fondo
items.description: 2023 James Beard winner. Hyper-local PR ingredients, modern tasting menu.
items.why_it_matters: #1 priority — highest editorial momentum in San Juan dining right now.

items.name: La Casita Blanca
items.description: The locals' canonical comida criolla answer. Classic PR home cooking.
items.why_it_matters: Reddit consensus #1 for authentic criollo — what locals send tourists to.

items.name: La Alcapurria Quemá
items.description: Top street food kiosk near La Placita. Alcapurrias, mofongo, beer.
items.why_it_matters: Constantly named by locals — the late-night Santurce circuit anchor.
